Astronomical scale tiers — the chart is a multi-scale diagram, not a linear map: 20 orders of magnitude separate Neptune's orbit from the observable universe, so distance compresses in three documented tiers while every direction stays astronomically true.

Galactic tier — 1 unit = 100 ly; the Milky Way disc (radius 520 units ≈ 52 000 ly) and its satellite dwarfs sit at real scale relative to each other. The Sun rests at 267 units ≈ 26 700 ly from the disc centre. Local-Group — beyond 1 Mly the scale drops to 800 ly/unit so M31 tier lands ~11 900 units out (true direction kept). Cosmic tier — beyond 10 Mly the scale drops to 20 000 ly/unit; superclusters and the observable-universe boundary shell clamp onto the far field (~46k units) inside the skybox.
